name: Can you install a zero-threshold or curbless tile shower for accessibility?

mainEntity.name: Can you install a zero-threshold or curbless tile shower for accessibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, installing curbless or barrier-free shower tile requires specialized planning, including recessing the subfloor or installing a pre-sloped linear drain pan so the shower floor sits completely flush with the bathroom floor. This design eliminates tripping hazards and allows roll-in access for mobility devices. At HH Remodeling, accessibility modifications are planned alongside custom tile setting to ensure proper floor pitch toward the drain, preventing water from escaping into the dry bathroom space while maintaining smooth transitions across the entryway.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, curbless tile showers require recessing the subfloor and using a sloped pan or linear drain so the floor remains flush while water drains properly.
